newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Delfood takes knock following yr results.
newsitem.headline: Delfood takes knock following yr results.

text.p: Shares in Del Monte Royal Foods Ltd (Delfoods) took a nine percent knock on Thursday to reach a record low as the market digested lower-than-expected year earnings released last week, traders said.
By 1550 GMT, the company's shares had dropped 30 cents, or 9.1 percent, to three rand as 8.2 million shares valued at 24.6 million rand changed hands.
"Del Foods has been coming off for quite a while. The results weren't as the market expected so it's been under pressure," a trader said.
Last Friday, Delfoods reported headline share earnings of 50.1 cents for the year ended November 30 versus 42.2 cents previously.
It pegged its dividend at 19 cents from 16 cents. Analysts had expected the company to report earnings per share of 52 cents with the dividend hiked to 19-22 cents.

Shares in Del Monte Corporation Ltd, which has a 46.5 percent investment in Delfoods, came off 25 cents, or 11.76 percent, to three rand after touching an all time low of 296 during the day. About 5.6 million shares worth over 17 million rand were traded.
"I don't think there's anything fundamentally wrong with the company. There seems to be a very big trade between two local players. It seems to be just a negotiated price," one trader said.
One trader said: "I don't think one should read too much into it".
